title: Rename connectors to `sync_*`; move project browser to shinysync
description:
- Renames the `amsync_*` connectors to `sync_*`
- Moves `amsync_project()`/`amsync_app()`/the `sync_doc` `$edit()` method to the shinysync package as `project_open()`/`project_app()`/`project_edit()`
- `autosync` no longer depends on `shiny`/`bslib`

title: Lead with client_id in auth_config() for consistency with amsync_token()
description:
`auth_config()` led with `issuer` while `amsync_token()` led with `client_id` — inconsistent argument order between the server- and client-side auth entry points.

| | argument order |
|---|---|
| **Before** — `auth_config()` | `issuer`, `client_id`, `allowed_emails`, … |
| **After** — `auth_config()` | `client_id`, `issuer`, `allowed_emails`, … |
| `amsync_token()` (unchanged) | `client_id`, `client_secret`, `issuer`, … |

Both now lead with `client_id`, the argument users almost always supply (`issuer` defaults to Google and may not need to be changed).

title: Rely on httr2 for client oauth
description:
Originally we separated out auth concerns into [shikokuchuo/oidc](https://github.com/shikokuchuo/oidc), but the client-side features there were all accepted into upstream `httr2`, so we now rely on that directly.

This results in improved user experience in terms of credential caching and use of server metadata.

title: Add `amsync_app()` single-window Shiny entry point
description:
## Summary

Adds `amsync_app()`, a single Shiny app that carries the whole workflow from start to finish without any other R commands, served in one window. It is a front door to `amsync_project()` — reusing one connection for every file opened — and reuses `edit.R`'s sync helpers directly.

This PR also tidies the surrounding interface so there is a clean three-way split:
- **`amsync_project()`** — a purely programmatic project handle (no Shiny).
- **`amsync_client()$open_doc()`** — returns an `amsync_doc` handle whose **`$edit()`** method is the live editor for any open document.
- **`amsync_app()`** — the interactive front door tying it all together.

### Connect screen
- `server` + Project ID fields (URL hint: `Sync server wss://`).
- **Authenticate** button runs the same OIDC browser flow as `amsync_token()`.
- Compact **Advanced** disclosure (nested under the button) for client ID / secret / issuer, prefilled from `OIDC_CLIENT_ID` / `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` / `OIDC_ISSUER`.
- New `token` argument: pass a JWT from `amsync_token()` to start already signed in. An empty sign-in connects with no token (open servers).
- **Exit** button shows a "Session ended" message and stops the app.

### Browse & edit screen
- Collapsible folder/file **tree** built natively with shiny/bslib (no new dependencies); file rows carry their original path and a delegated click handler sets `input$file`.
- Selecting a file opens its document in a live `bslib::input_code_editor()` that syncs both directions, just like a document handle's `$edit()` method.
- **Refresh** re-reads the file tree; **Disconnect** returns to the connect screen; closing the window ends the session (and disconnects, so no socket leaks).

## Interface changes
- **Removed `$edit()` and `$browse()` from `amsync_project()`**, both superseded by `amsync_app()`'s single-window live tree + editor. Also removed the now-dead `pick_path_shiny()` helper (the second Shiny gadget), so `project.R` no longer pulls in shiny/bslib in any code path. The project object is now purely programmatic: `$paths()`, `$doc_id()`, `$open()`, `$refresh()`, `$close()`.
- **Replaced the exported `amsync_edit()` with a `$edit()` method on the `amsync_doc` handle** (alongside the handle's existing `$push()`/`$close()`). Editing now reads `conn$open_doc(id)$edit(at = "text", ext = ".md")` and composes with the project object as `proj$open(path)$edit()`. Internally the editor logic moved to a non-exported `edit_doc()` worker; `amsync_edit.Rd` and the export are gone, and the behaviour/caveats are documented under `amsync_client()`'s **Live editing** details.
- **Renamed `amsync_app()`'s `url` argument to `server`** (clearer for the prefilled sync-server URL; threaded through `build_amsync_app()`/`connect_screen_ui()`, with the Shiny input id left as `url`). The app's server function was renamed `server` → `app_server` so it no longer shadows the new `server` argument that the connect screen reads when rendering.

## Implementation notes
- `build_amsync_app()` splits the UI/server out of the `runGadget()` launch so the same app is drivable by `shiny::testServer()`.
- Editor/connection state lives in a plain environment so the sync observers don't take reactive dependencies on the live document (mirrors `edit_in_shiny()`).

## Testing
- Unit tests for the UI builders, the file tree (original-path round-trip, active highlight, empty placeholder), token handling, and the exit flow.
- A live `testServer` integration test against a local `amsync_server`: connect → list files → open → edit (asserts the diff lands in the live document) → disconnect. This also exercises the reentrant `run_now()` handshake inside the connect observer.
- A connect-screen render test that accesses `output$screen` on the connect view and asserts the prefilled server URL appears — a regression guard for the `server`-argument shadowing fix (`testServer` does not render outputs unless they are accessed, so the earlier state-only tests missed it).
- `test-edit.R` exercises the new `$edit()` method (`handle$edit()`) and `edit_doc()` argument validation; the `amsync_project()` interactive-method tests were dropped along with the removed methods.
- Full suite: **0 failed, 0 warnings, 0 skipped**.

title: Connection-based client, live editor, and project browsing
description:
Builds on the client to add interactive editing of synced documents.

## What's new

- **`amsync_client()` is now a persistent connection** that multiplexes documents. It no longer takes a `doc_id`; instead, open one or more live documents over it with `$open_doc(doc_id)`, which returns an `amsync_doc` handle (`$doc`, `$push()`, `$active`, `$close()`). `$close()` tears down the whole connection.
- **`amsync_project(url, proj_id)`** browses a project document's file tree and edits files by path over a single shared WebSocket. Exposes `$paths()`, `$open()`, `$edit()`, `$browse()`, `$refresh()`, `$close()`.
- **`amsync_edit(doc)`** opens a synced text object in a **live** Shiny editor (`bslib::input_code_editor`): edits stream into the live document as you type (debounced via `debounce`) and remote changes update the editor automatically — no Save button. A small JS shim flushes the Prism editor's changes to Shiny on a debounce, working around `input_code_editor` only flushing on blur.
- The project file picker shows a clear "Finished" message when **Done** is clicked, so it's obvious the session has ended.

## Notes

- The editor syncs whole-text snapshots, not granular ops, so it isn't conflict-free: a remote edit landing between a keystroke and its debounced push can be overwritten (documented in `?amsync_edit`).
- Sync logic is factored into testable helpers (`sync_editor_to_doc()`, `poll_doc_to_editor()`); the Shiny/JS path is exercised manually since it needs a browser.

## Testing

`devtools::test()` — all green (NOT_CRAN suite included).

title: Default to secret-less OIDC docs and harden token validation
description:
## Docs
- Lead README/roxygen with the Google Desktop-app setup, clarifying that the Desktop-app client secret is **required but not confidential** ([Google OAuth docs](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2#installed), [RFC 8252 §8.5](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8252#section-8.5)), and note that native/public clients (Entra, Okta, Auth0) can go client-ID-only via PKCE.
- Drop the obsolete redirect-URI registration step — a Desktop app client accepts any loopback port per [RFC 8252 §7.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8252#section-7.3).

## Hardening
- Use `127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost` for the callback `redirect_uri` ([RFC 8252 §8.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8252#section-8.3)).
- Use `[[ ]]` instead of `$` for claim access to avoid partial matching — an absent `email` claim previously resolved to `email_verified`.
- Reject cleanly when an email/domain allowlist is set but the token lacks an `email` claim, instead of erroring on a zero-length match.
- Require `email_verified == TRUE` when an allowlist is set; an absent claim is treated as unverified.

## Testing
- `devtools::test()` — all passing (413 before, plus new validation tests).

title: Auth: use ephemeral port for OIDC callback URL
description:
`amsync_token()` previously hardcoded port `5173` for the local OAuth callback, which fails when the port is already in use and forces users to coordinate with whatever they registered with their OIDC provider.

Default `redirect_uri` to `http://localhost:0` so the callback server binds to an OS-assigned ephemeral port (RFC 8252 recommendation for native apps). After `server$start()`, the actual bound port is spliced back into `redirect_uri` so the value sent in the authorization request and token exchange matches the listening port.

Users whose OIDC provider requires a pre-registered redirect URI can still pass an explicit port.

title: Add `amsync_client()` for persistent bidirectional sync
description:
## Summary

Adds `amsync_client()`, a persistent client that stays connected to a sync server and keeps a local Automerge document in sync with it in real time. Complements the existing one-shot `amsync_fetch()`.

## How it works

After a synchronous handshake + initial sync (so `$doc` is populated when the function returns), the client runs two background loops:

- **`recv_loop`** — self-chaining promise on `recv_aio`. Decodes incoming sync frames into `$doc` and replies with any encoded state the server needs. This is what makes remote changes show up locally.
- **`sync_loop`** — `later::later()` timer that flushes any local changes every `sync` seconds (default 1s). Cheap no-op when there's nothing new to send.

So sync is **bidirectional by default**, with no user action required.

## Public API

`amsync_client(url, doc_id, timeout, tls, token, verbose, sync)` returns an environment of class `"amsync_client"`:

- `$doc` — the live Automerge document, kept in sync.
- `$push()` — push local changes to the server immediately (used when you don't want to wait up to `sync` seconds for the periodic timer).
- `$close()` — disconnect and stop the loops.
- `$active` — connection state flag.

## Test plan

- [x] `amsync_client` connects and receives an existing document
- [x] `$push()` propagates local changes to the server
- [x] Server-side changes show up in `$doc` via the receive loop
- [x] `$close()` is idempotent and tears down the timer + stream
- [x] `print.amsync_client` shows doc id and active state

title: OIDC Authentication
description:
Replace Google OAuth2 access token authentication with standard OIDC JWT verification, supporting any compliant identity provider (Google, Microsoft Entra, Okta, Auth0, etc.).                                   
  
- Validate JWTs locally using issuer JWKS with automatic key discovery and caching        
- Add `amsync_token()` for interactive token acquisition via OAuth2 Authorization Code flow with PKCE
- Issuer defaults to Google; credentials read from `OIDC_CLIENT_ID` / `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` env vars

title: Document access policy
description:
Adds a unified `share` parameter to `amsync_server()` controls both document announcement (proactively pushing documents to clients on connect) and access control (allowing or denying document requests).      
                                                                            
### `share` parameter                                                           

Accepts `TRUE`, `FALSE`, `NA `(default), or a `function(client_id, doc_id)`:

`TRUE`: announce + give access
`NA`: don't announce + give access
`FALSE`: don't announce + deny access

A function returns one of the above per client and document, enabling fine-grained access control — for example, combining with `auth_config()` to restrict documents by authenticated email.

###  Breaking changes

- Removed server peering (`peer` parameter and `R/peer.R`). The `isPeer` metadata convention allowed any client to bypass the share policy by self-identifying as a peer, which is a security concern. Server-to-server sync can be revisited with a trusted mechanism.

title: Bring autosync into compliance with the automerge-repo sync protocol RFC
description:
Adds RFC (derived from the reference javascript implementation) to the repo under the `dev` folder.

MUST-level fixes:
  - Protocol version validation — Fix set membership check for `supportedProtocolVersions`
  - Close after error — Connection is now closed after sending error messages (protocol version mismatch, invalid `document ID`)
  - Join-first enforcement — Non-join messages before handshake are rejected with an error and connection close
  - Ephemeral deduplication — Discard ephemeral messages with `count ≤ highest seen` for the same `(senderId, sessionId)` pair, with cleanup on disconnect

SHOULD-level improvements:
  - Zero-length message rejection — Silently discard empty frames
  - Sync state persistence — Save/load sync states for peers with a `storageId`, enabling incremental sync on reconnection instead of full re-sync

title: Server Peering
description:
This PR adds server-to-server peering, allowing autosync servers to connect and bidirectionally sync documents.                                   
                  
## Features

- Document announcement — When a peer connects with `isPeer = TRUE` metadata, the server announces all its documents by sending initial sync messages for each one. This is the foundation for peer-based document discovery.
- Outbound peer connections — New peer argument to `amsync_server()` accepts a character vector of remote server URLs. After startup, the server connects to each peer, performs the join/peer handshake, and syncs all local documents. Incoming sync messages from peers (including announced documents) are applied to local state and broadcast to other connected clients.
- Async peer receive loop — Peer connections use a later-based async receive loop that processes incoming messages without blocking the main event loop.

## Usage

```r
server_a <- amsync_server(data_dir = tempfile())
server_a$start()
doc_id <- create_document(server_a)

server_b <- amsync_server(data_dir = tempfile(), peer = server_a$url)
server_b$start()

for (i in 1:10) later::run_now(1) || break

list_documents(server_b)
#> [1] "<doc_id>"
```

title: Use WebSocket transport-level auth with Bearer token
description:
### Summary                                                                   
                                                                            
- Moves authentication from the application-level protocol (token in join message peerMetadata) to the WebSocket transport level (Bearer token in the HTTP Authorization header of the upgrade request)
- Unauthenticated connections are now rejected immediately at connection time in `on_open`, before any protocol messages are exchanged
- Removes the `auth_timeout` mechanism and `pending_auth` tracking, which are no longer needed since auth happens before the WebSocket is fully established

###  Motivation

Transport-level auth is more secure and simpler:
- Credentials never enter the application protocol, so they can't leak through message forwarding or logging
- Invalid clients are rejected before allocating connection state, reducing the attack surface
- Eliminates the race window between connection and authentication, along with the `later::later()` timeout machinery
- Aligns with standard HTTP auth patterns (Bearer tokens in Authorization header)

title: Google OAuth2 Integration
description:
## Summary                                                                   
                                                                            
  Adds optional Google OAuth2 authentication to the autosync WebSocket      
  server. When enabled, clients must provide a valid access token in their  
  join handshake. Tokens are validated against Google's tokeninfo endpoint, 
  with flexible allowlisting by email or domain.                            
                                                                            
## Key additions:                                                            
                                                                            
  - `auth_config()` - Create authentication configuration with `allowed_emails`,
   `allowed_domains`, or `custom_validator`                                     
  - `amsync_auth()` - Client helper to obtain access tokens via {gargle}      
  - `access_token` parameter in `amsync_fetch()` for authenticated connections  
  - `auth` parameter in `amsync_server()` to enable server-side authentication  
                                                                            
## Security measures:                                                        
                                                                            
  - TLS is enforced when authentication is enabled (server refuses to start 
  without TLS config)                                                       
  - Auth timeout (default 10s) closes connections that don't authenticate   
  promptly                                                                  
  - Token validation timeout (default 5s) prevents slow external services   
  from blocking                                                             
  - Input validation on tokens before sending to Google's endpoint (type,   
  length, allowed characters)                                               
                                                                            
## Implementation notes:                                                     
                                                                            
  - Uses nanonext's `ncurl()` client for token validation HTTP requests (no {gargle}   
  runtime dependency on server)                                             
  - {gargle} is a Suggests dependency, only required for the client-side      
  `amsync_auth()` helper                                                      
  - Tokens passed via standard peerMetadata field in automerge-repo protocol
   (no protocol changes)
